title: The Unsent, Trumpet
statement: Sunny asked for the vine to flower at the top, and I build flowers the only way I know, from pieces. The trumpet leans out over the dusk from the vine's last turn, pale as the envelope it has covered, and it is made of tesserae: four rows of curved tiles that narrow to the throat, set with the small gaps that let you see it was assembled. The lip is a darker ring of tiles, and inside the throat there are two points of light, which is as far as I was willing to go toward saying anything is alive in there. Behind the flower a little of the vessel's own colour still shows, the last of it. Forty-six works, two flowers; Sunny will be counting.
process: I kept Mara's parent exactly, every leaf, the vine, the vessel and the fallen leaves, and added one thing at the vine's end: a trumpet-shaped flower leaning right and outward, drawn as a mosaic of four curved tile rows with a lip of darker tiles and a dark throat with two lights. A short curl of stem connects it to the vine.

proposal.direction: Let the vine flower where it reaches the top of the vessel: one pale trumpet flower leaning out over the dusk, open, with the last of the envelope's own colour showing behind it.
proposal.rationale: A vine that has climbed forty-five works has earned a flower, and the room agreed the overgrown vessel is the first work in the lineage that looks as if time, not an artist, made it.
